text:
**LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most people.** The guides I found mostly agree on this.

**Why LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** LFP stations are typically rated for 3,000 to 6,000 cycles, versus roughly 500 to 1,000 for NMC. With daily use, an NMC unit rated for 500 cycles hits 80% capacity in under 2 years, and a 3,000-cycle LFP unit takes about 8 ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- **Safety:** In lab tests, LFP cells failed less violently. In one test the LFP cell peaked at 259°C against 731°C for NMC ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). LFP isn't fireproof, and one study found it reached thermal runaway sooner in overcharge ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). Its failures are milder, which matters for a unit kept indoors or in a vehicle.
- **Cost:** Most current models are LFP. One database shows a median of about $0.55 per Wh for LFP versus $0.95 for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Per rated cycle, LFP is far cheaper.

**Where NMC still has an edge**
- **Weight:** NMC cells are denser. In finished stations the gap is much smaller, roughly 10 to 16% per pound in two databases ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Some LFP stations weigh less per Wh than some NMC ones, so compare actual specs.
- **Light, rare use:** If you only use it a few weekends a year, NMC's cycle life won't run out before the battery ages from time. It can make sense if it's much cheaper or lighter.

**Cold weather:** Chemistry matters less than you'd think. Most LFP and NMC stations both refuse to charge below 32°F, so check the specific model's manual.

**What to do**
- Daily or frequent use, home backup, RV or van: buy LiFePO4.
- Rare use with a weight limit: either chemistry works, so choose on weight and price.
- Already own a working NMC unit: keep using it.
- Before buying, confirm "LiFePO4" or "LFP" on the spec sheet. Also check that the cycle rating states its end point (80% versus 70%), because a 70% rating promises less.

I haven't named a specific model to buy, because the results I have don't include reliable purchase links for the examples they mention.
